slides.teach: A ledger designed for broad visibility and verification of recorded transactions or entries.

course.learn: A ledger designed for broad visibility and verification of recorded transactions or entries.

blocks.title: Blockchain and public ledger are related, not identical
items: A blockchain describes the linked-record structure; it can exist in public or permissioned environments.
Example: A private consortium may use blockchain without exposing all records publicly.
The defining idea is that ledger entries are broadly viewable.
Example: Anyone can inspect transactions on a public ledger.
blocks.example: Memory: Blockchain = structure · Open public ledger = visibility.

questions.q: Which term describes a ledger whose entries can be broadly inspected by participants or the public?
questions.explanation: An open public ledger is designed for broad visibility of recorded entries.

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes blockchain from an open public ledger?
choices: Blockchain describes a linked-record structure; an open public ledger describes broad visibility of ledger entries
They are always exactly the same thing
An open public ledger is a type of private key
Blockchain is only a certificate status protocol
questions.explanation: Blockchain is a data structure/technology; open public ledger refers to visibility.

questions.q: A consortium uses blockchain internally but does not expose all records publicly. Which statement is correct?
choices: A blockchain does not have to be an open public ledger
The system is therefore not using cryptography
A private blockchain cannot use hashes
questions.explanation: Blockchain can be used in public or permissioned environments.
